implementation_scope: Additive change to the existing browser-only OpenCV.js tracing pipeline. Do not replace OCR, leader assignment, SlimSAM segmentation, tactile layout, braille encoding, SVG export, or STL export.

problem_statement.observed_failure: The uploaded labeled anatomical cross-section is transcribed correctly, but the tactile trace omits important low-contrast outlines and lighter internal structures. The output is biased toward the darkest/highest-contrast strokes.
visual_evidence_to_recover: The continuous outer shell / body silhouette, including its curved perimeter.
The outline of the large lower foot region.
Long, light internal anatomical boundaries and folds.
Thin but continuous structural contours that are visually weaker than the darkest black strokes.
problem_statement.do_not_assume: Do not treat every pale pixel, shading transition, OCR glyph, leader line, stipple, hatch, or paper artifact as a tactile feature.

primary_objective: Recover more semantically useful diagram structure at adjustable sensitivity while keeping the final tactile graphic sparse, separable by touch, and compliant with the project's existing physical spacing and braille-placement checks.
preserve_existing_behavior: Keep the current Detailed and Simplified style choices and their meanings.
Keep OCR text detection, text-box erasure, leader-line detection/chaining, and leader-line removal from structural tracing.
Keep label-guided SAM masks and the existing bold hierarchy for boundaries of named parts.
Keep the current silhouette, part, texture, braille, key-page, and export stages.
Keep all processing local in the browser; do not add server calls, paid APIs, or Python runtime dependencies.
Keep existing defaults visually close to current output unless the user explicitly changes sensitivity.

likely_sensitivity_bottlenecks: app/js/lineart.js: structureLines uses fixed region-boundary contrast (step defaults to 18), fixed black-hat/top-hat stroke thresholds (35 and 50), a fixed 7x7 morphology kernel, and a minimum stroke length proportional to the working image diagonal.
app/js/pipeline.js: foregroundMask uses a fixed RGB distance threshold (>28), then morphology OPEN/CLOSE and small-component removal; faint outer contours can be lost before later tracing stages.
app/js/pipeline.js: lineArtMask uses fixed Canny thresholds (60, 160) for Detailed edges.
app/js/tactile.js: Detailed removes fragments under 4 mm; Simplified merges nearby strokes at a 3 mm scale, thins them, and removes fragments under 12.5 mm.
app/js/tactile.js: braille placement uses a 3 mm clearance occupancy grid; this must remain authoritative when additional lines are introduced.
diagnosis_from_current_source.instruction: Treat these as source-inspection findings, not proof that any single threshold is the sole cause. Instrument intermediate masks and test the uploaded image plus the existing sample/evaluation set before choosing final thresholds.

behavior: Expose the control in the existing options area without removing the Detailed/Simplified style selector.
Changing sensitivity should recompute tracing/layout from the already loaded image and analysis data where feasible; do not rerun OCR or model downloads unless required.
Show a short explanatory note: higher sensitivity recovers lighter and weaker contours, but may add clutter; tactile spacing and braille checks still apply.
Persist the selected value in in-memory UI state for the current session. Do not add localStorage or remote persistence unless the project already has an established settings mechanism.

proposed_tracing_strategy.principle: Use multiple complementary edge candidates and rank them; do not merely lower one global threshold.

candidate_layers.name: silhouette_recovery
candidate_layers.purpose: Recover the complete outside contour of the drawing and major connected regions even when their boundary is faint.
method: Build a robust page-background estimate from border pixels, but do not assume every white-looking pixel inside the drawing is background.
Use a tolerant foreground candidate mask with local contrast or luminance/chroma distance, plus connected-component and contour continuity checks.
Recover the dominant outer contour independently from interior dark-stroke detection.
Prefer long, closed, smooth contours enclosing substantial drawing area; reject isolated page noise.
Retain the existing OCR text-box exclusions and leader-line exclusions.

candidate_layers.name: strong_edges
candidate_layers.purpose: Keep clearly printed structural strokes and strong region boundaries.
candidate_layers.method: Retain current edge and region-boundary candidates as the high-confidence layer.

candidate_layers.name: weak_edges
candidate_layers.purpose: Recover light pencil/ink contours and low-contrast internal structures.
method: Add a lower-threshold edge candidate pass (for example, Canny-style hysteresis with independently configurable low/high thresholds) and/or local-gradient thresholding.
Use local contrast normalization or a multi-scale gradient so faint lines are detectable without globally amplifying page texture.
Keep weak candidates only when they have sufficient length, continuity, curvature consistency, enclosure, or proximity to a known structural boundary / named-part mask.
Avoid treating broad smooth shading gradients as edges; require a localized gradient ridge or persistent contour across scales.

candidate_layers.name: region_boundaries
candidate_layers.purpose: Retain boundaries between meaningful diagram regions even when their luminance difference is modest.
method: Make the current Lab boundary step threshold sensitivity-aware.
Keep the existing strategy of down-weighting lightness in colour clustering so shading does not dominate.
Reject boundaries that merely follow smooth tonal bands or tiny segmentation regions.

candidate_fusion: Combine candidates with provenance/confidence metadata before rasterizing the final mask.
Rank outer silhouette and long continuous anatomical contours above isolated high-frequency details.
Use named-part SAM masks to promote relevant boundary candidates, not to indiscriminately fill or outline every pixel inside a mask.
Deduplicate overlapping candidates and join only short gaps when the continuation direction and local evidence agree.
Keep the outer silhouette as a distinct layer so later simplification cannot erase it.

sensitivity_mapping.requirement: Map the 0-100 UI value to named, testable parameters in one centralized configuration function. Avoid scattering magic numbers across files.
mapping_guidance: Increasing sensitivity should lower weak-edge and local-contrast thresholds gradually, not linearly force all thresholds to zero.
Keep strong-edge thresholds stable or nearly stable so high-confidence geometry is not destabilized.
Reduce the minimum accepted stroke length only moderately as sensitivity rises; retain a hard tactile-size filter during layout.
Use conservative defaults around sensitivity 55, then tune against the supplied diagram and the repository's existing sample/evaluation corpus.
Clamp all derived thresholds to safe ranges and validate values before passing them into OpenCV.js.

rules: Do not solve missed outlines by raising every detected edge.
Do not reduce the existing 3 mm braille clearance or allow braille dots to collide with new structural lines.
Preserve the existing distinction between Detailed and Simplified: Detailed can retain more meaningful detail; Simplified must aggressively merge close lines and remove sub-12.5 mm fragments.
Apply density-aware pruning after candidate recovery and before final braille placement.
When local line density is too high, preserve in this order: outer silhouette; long closed boundaries; boundaries of labeled parts; long continuous internal anatomy; short secondary detail.
Remove or merge low-confidence parallel lines that cannot be distinguished at tactile scale.
Do not add textures to compensate for missing outlines; retain the existing maximum of five textures and texture inset.
Let the existing braille occupancy grid relocate labels or use its existing key/knockout fallback. Never silently shrink braille or its clearance to fit more lines.

If line recovery makes a label impossible to place safely, retain the label through the existing key-page/placement behavior and report the collision in diagnostics rather than sacrificing braille legibility.
density_metrics_to_record: number of candidate edges before pruning
number and total length of retained edges by confidence tier
percentage of figure area with line spacing under 3 mm
number of labels placed and number with full 3 mm clearance
whether the outer silhouette was recovered as a continuous contour

implementation_plan.title: Centralize sensitivity configuration
details: Add a pure helper (preferably in app/js/lineart.js or a small app/js/tracing-config.js module) that converts sensitivity 0-100 into validated tracing parameters.
Give the helper stable defaults matching current behavior as closely as possible.
Pass the resulting config through analyze/lineArtMask/structureLines without introducing global mutable state.

implementation_plan.title: Recover silhouette and weak contours
details: Separate outer silhouette recovery from dark thin-stroke extraction.
Add a weak-edge pass using local contrast or multi-threshold hysteresis.
Retain strong and weak candidates separately until confidence ranking and pruning are complete.
Ensure OCR boxes and assigned leader lines are excluded from every relevant candidate layer.

implementation_plan.title: Add tactile-aware candidate pruning
details: Rank candidates by geometry, confidence, continuity, and semantic relevance.
Promote the outer contour and long named-part boundaries.
Prune dense parallel/noisy edges before passing masks into buildLayout.
Keep the current Detailed and Simplified downstream operations and their physical dimensions.

implementation_plan.title: Expose the UI control
details: Add a labeled 0-100 sensitivity slider and concise helper text in the existing tracing/options UI.
On slider change, regenerate tracing and tactile layout from the current image; avoid rerunning OCR/SAM if the architecture allows a tracing-only recompute.
Display the chosen sensitivity in the UI and include it in diagnostics.

implementation_plan.title: Keep validation authoritative
details: Reuse checkAll and the existing tactile measurements.
Add weak-edge retention and clutter metrics to the analysis diagnostics.

Do not mark a result successful merely because more pixels were traced; success requires improved outline recall without regressions in braille clearance, line spacing, fragments, or print-text removal.

acceptance_criteria: On the supplied anatomical diagram, the outer shell is represented by a continuous, clearly traceable raised contour.
The large foot boundary and several long, light internal anatomical boundaries are recovered where they are visually continuous and structurally meaningful.
Purple printed labels and their OCR boxes do not become raised text-shaped marks.
Leader lines are not duplicated as structural anatomy; the existing leader treatment remains the thinnest line class.
Sensitivity changes visibly alter weak-edge recovery in a predictable monotonic direction.
At sensitivity 55, the result is more complete than the current failure while remaining sparse enough for tactile exploration.
At sensitivity 100, extra detail may appear, but density pruning and tactile checks still prevent uncontrolled clutter.
Braille remains legible and retains at least the existing 3 mm clearance behavior.
Simplified mode retains its 3 mm merge spacing and 12.5 mm minimum primary-line filtering.
Existing sample diagrams continue to run in-browser with no server dependency and no regression in OCR label recall or text removal.
No uncaught OpenCV.js Mat/resource leaks are introduced; all temporary Mats are deleted on every success/error path.
test_plan: Use the supplied image as a regression fixture and compare current output with sensitivity values 0, 25, 55, 75, and 100.
Run npm run eval and the repository's recall script on the existing sample corpus.
Inspect intermediate masks for foreground, silhouette, strong edges, weak edges, fused candidates, and final tactile lines.
Record checker results for narrow gaps, short fragments, print text remaining, braille placement, and braille clearance at every sensitivity setting.
Test both Detailed and Simplified styles at low, default, and high sensitivity.
Test a low-contrast outline diagram, a high-contrast line drawing, a shaded diagram, and a diagram with dense labels.
Verify changing sensitivity does not trigger OCR/SAM model reloads unnecessarily.
engineering_notes: Use JavaScript and the project's existing OpenCV.js primitives; do not introduce a Python image-processing service.
Prefer deterministic classical image processing over adding another ML model.
Do not hard-code the uploaded image's dimensions, exact anatomy, or coordinates.
Keep performance suitable for the current browser workflow; reuse grayscale/Lab intermediates where practical.
Guard against empty masks, tiny images, all-white images, and OpenCV.js allocation failures.
Add comments explaining each sensitivity parameter in image-space or physical tactile units.
Keep the existing source organization unless a small isolated tracing configuration module materially improves maintainability.
deliverable: Implement the above as a focused, reviewable JavaScript change. First report the files to be changed and the parameter mapping; then implement, run the available tests, and summarize measured improvements and any remaining limitations. Do not claim tests passed unless they were actually run.
